item.research_question: How does modifying grain boundary morphology from straight to serrated affect the hot ductility drop, tensile fracture strain, and creep rupture life of a selective laser melting (SLM) fabricated precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloy at elevated temperatures?
item.material_system: Al8Co35Cr18Ni34Ti3Nb2Zr0.005B0.01 (at.%) high-entropy alloy (SLMHEA) with fcc γ matrix and L12 γ′ precipitates
item.processing_route: Selective laser melting (SLM) with 270 W laser power, 1000 mm/s scanning speed, 75 μm hatch distance, and 200°C pre-heat; followed by solution heat treatment at 1120°C for 1 h; HT-1 involved air-cooling to room temperature then aging at 750°C for 48 h; HT-2 involved slow cooling at 1°C/min to 1000°C then air-cooling to room temperature followed by aging at 750°C for 48 h
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests at 25°C and 650°C with strain rate 10−3 s−1; creep tests at 650°C/650 MPa; molecular dynamic simulations at 650°C under 650 MPa load
key_findings: Serrated grain boundary increased tensile fracture strain at 650°C by a factor of 3.5 (from 1.8% to 6.3%)
Serrated grain boundary increased creep rupture life at 650°C/650 MPa by a factor of 400 (from 0.58 h to 274 h)
Minimum creep strain rate decreased by 96% in the serrated sample (from 6.4 × 10−6 s−1 to 2.4 × 10−7 s−1)
Average strain at triple junctions reduced from 28% in straight grain boundaries to 11% in serrated grain boundaries (reduction >50%)
HT-2 sample (serrated) exhibited 0.45% creep fracture strain compared to 0.03% for HT-1 (straight)
Grain boundary serration wavelength was 3.29 ± 0.38 μm and amplitude was 1.69 ± 0.24 μm in HT-2 samples
Coarse γ′ precipitates in HT-2 had an average size of 1.8 μm, compared to 60.1 nm in HT-1
Geometric factor ϕ for creep rate calculation was 0.017 for serrated boundaries versus 1 for straight boundaries
item.mechanism: The slow cooling process coarsens L12 γ′ precipitates which interact with mobile grain boundaries via the Zener drag effect, pinning them and causing undulation (serration). This serrated morphology distributes strains more evenly, reduces local strain concentration at triple junctions by over 50%, acts as a crack deflector to retard intergranular crack propagation, and provides resistance against shear parallel to the grain boundary surface.
item.limitations: The thermodynamic database predictions for σ phase, C14 Laves phase, B2 phase, and borides did not match experimental observations, likely due to database inaccuracies or non-equilibrium conditions; the study focuses on a single alloy composition and specific heat treatment parameters.
item.future_work: The study suggests providing a guideline to develop future high-entropy alloys and design post heat treatments for elevated temperature applications, though specific future experiments are not detailed beyond this general recommendation.
quotes: serrated grain boundary could render a significant increase in tensile fracture strain and creep rupture life by a factor of 3.5 and 400, respectively.

The serrated grain boundary could be achieved by reducing the cooling rate of solution heat treatment, which allowed the coarsening of L12 structured γ′ precipitates to interfere with mobile grain boundaries, resulting in undulation of the grain boundary morphology.
Simulation results demonstrated that severely localized strains at triple junctions, by contrast strains were more homogeneous distributed along serrated grain boundaries.
